what_its_for: Filgrastim-sndz helps your body make more white blood cells called neutrophils. These cells fight infections. Your doctor may prescribe this medicine if you are receiving chemotherapy, have had a bone marrow transplant, have a condition where your body does not make enough white blood cells, or if you are donating stem cells for someone else.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous) or into a vein (intravenous). Your doctor, nurse, or pharmacist will show you exactly how to inject it yourself at home if needed. Always use a new needle and syringe each time. Inject into the stomach area (abdomen), upper thigh, or upper arm. Do not inject into skin that is bruised, red, tender, or hard. Rotate injection sites so you do not use the exact same spot each time. Never shake the vial or prefilled syringe, as this can damage the medicine.
dosing: Your dose depends on your weight, your medical condition, and why you are taking this medicine. Your doctor will calculate the right dose for you. It is usually given once a day. Follow your doctor's instructions exactly and do not change your dose on your own. Use it at the same time each day to help you remember.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, call your doctor or nurse right away for instructions. Do not double up or take two doses to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, contact your healthcare team before giving yourself another injection.
storage: Store filgrastim-sndz in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it. If it accidentally freezes, thaw it once in the refrigerator — do not use it if it has been frozen and thawed more than once. You may keep it at room temperature (up to 86°F or 30°C) for no more than 24 hours. Throw away any medicine left at room temperature after 24 hours. Keep out of reach of children. Dispose of used needles and syringes in an FDA-approved sharps container right away.
what_to_avoid: Do not use filgrastim-sndz within 24 hours before or 24 hours after receiving chemotherapy, unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Avoid shaking the medicine. Do not use it if the liquid looks cloudy, discolored, or contains particles. Avoid injecting into areas of skin that are irritated, bruised, or have any skin conditions.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you have: sudden or severe pain in your upper left stomach area or left shoulder (this could be a sign of a serious spleen problem); difficulty breathing, fast heartbeat, or rash (signs of a possible allergic reaction); pain in your bones or muscles that is severe and not getting better; signs of infection such as fever, chills, or sore throat; unusual swelling in your legs or ankles; pain or redness at the injection site that does not go away; or if you feel very tired, short of breath, or look pale (signs of a possible blood cell disorder).
when_it_works: Filgrastim-sndz usually starts working within 1 to 2 days, and your white blood cell counts typically begin to rise within a few days of starting treatment. Your doctor will do blood tests to check how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep all your lab appointments so your doctor can monitor your blood counts and adjust your treatment if needed.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine during pregnancy or breastfeeding is not fully known. Tell your doctor if you have sickle cell disease, as this medicine may cause serious complications in people with that condition. If you have kidney or liver problems, let your doctor know, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Older adults and children can use this medicine, but your doctor will carefully choose the right dose based on your specific situation.
